artwork_date: Painted in December 1951, in France, this work is accompanied by a certificate of authenticity issued by the Fondation Zao Wou-Ki. This fall, Phillips and Capella Hotel Group debut their Living Art partnership with an extraordinary offering for the successful bidder of a work by the renowned Chinese abstract master Zao Wou-Ki in Phillips' Modern & Contemporary Art Evening Sale in Hong Kong on 30 September. Ahead of the sale, the painting was unveiled at Capella Taipei as part of an intimate private preview showcasing highlights from Phillips' upcoming Hong Kong auctions. The acquisition of Sans titre (La Théière) by Zao Wou-Ki will come with a unique experience that complements the rarity and beauty of this artwork. The successful bidder is welcomed to Capella Taipei for a two-night stay at one of its well-appointed suites, complemented by a Capella Curates itinerary created entirely around them — never to be repeated or offered to another guest. "Ammolite" is the name given to the colourful and wonderful Ammonite fossils found in the famous Bear Paw Formation in Southern Alberta, Canada. Their shells underwent a unique fossilization process over 75 million years. Exposure to pressure, temperature and geographic location caused the shell to mineralize into a rainbow of iridescent colours similar to opalization. The specimens are mined on the Native American Black Foot reservation, who themselves operate and oversee the excavation and production. Since 1981 Ammolite is recognized as a gemstone by the CIBJO Colored Stones Commission. The present specimen is very well preserved and complete showing a wide range of the most vivid and rare colorization. This particular specimen shows a high gloss coating, very good inflation and exceptional red and green colour as well as intact nacre to both sides. A fine and huge specimen for the knowledgeable collector. Measurements 66 x 69cm (26 x 27 1/8in)
